knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The test label and its next due date are read before any use. Running a machine to listen to it, or taping a flex, are both ruled out by the lesson.
The socket is switched off first, then the machine is unplugged. The reverse order leaves the machine live at the plug.
A damaged flex is a fault. The machine is tagged, unplugged and reported. Taping the cut or running it on a lower speed both leave the hazard in place.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied machine, the learner reads the test label, states the next due date and states whether the machine may be used.
Given a supplied machine with a planted fault (such as a nicked flex), the learner finds the fault during a hand-run of the flex, stops the machine, tags it and states the report step.
The learner connects and disconnects a supplied machine using the socket-switch sequence, with the assessor observing both steps.
On a supplied floor section, the learner routes the flex behind them while operating, with no part of the cable crossing the path of the head.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks (three questions, so all three must be correct to reach 80%; flagged for review). Practical sign-off is separate: the assessor signs off each practical criterion as observed.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Pre-use check record completed by the learner
Fault tag and report for the planted fault
stopWorkCriteria: Learner plugs in or unplugs with the socket switched on
Learner uses a machine with a damaged flex, cut, bare wire or tape repair
Learner uses a machine whose test date has passed
Learner attempts to open a casing or repair wiring
